slot.brief: Simplify a product of complex numbers given in polar/rectangular form; find the modulus and argument of the result

stem: The principal argument of the complex number $\dfrac{(1+i)^2}{1-i\sqrt{3}}$ is
notes: from question bank g01f8c5589b4f (verified in job 20261127-122012-292e)
working:
$(1+i)^2 = 2i$ so argument $\pi/2$. $1-i\sqrt{3}=2e^{-i\pi/3}$, argument $-\pi/3$. Division subtracts arguments: $\frac{\pi}{2} - \left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{5\pi}{6}$.

Independent check: \((1+i)^2=2i\), with argument \(\pi/2\). The denominator has argument \(-\pi/3\), so the quotient's principal argument is \(\pi/2-(-\pi/3)=5\pi/6\).
solution:
Using $\text{Arg}(z_1/z_2)=\text{Arg}(z_1)-\text{Arg}(z_2)$, we have $(1+i)^2=2i$ with argument $\frac{\pi}{2}$, and $1-i\sqrt{3}$ with argument $-\frac{\pi}{3}$.
$$\text{Arg}[0m\left(\frac{(1+i)^2}{1-i\sqrt{3}}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}-\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{5\pi}{6}.$$
